incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one layer of Bitget's three-tier hot wallet system and drained the platform's cryptocurrency reserve used for customer transactions.
incidents.impact: Approximately $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from the Singapore-based trading platform — the largest crypto heist of 2026. Bitget confirmed the breach and said remaining hot wallet layers were unaffected.

incidents.victim: NeedyMantis targets: telecom, universities, government contractors, IGOs
incidents.vector: Post-compromise deployment of NeedyMantis modular malware via DLL sideloading using legitimate software packages (Poedit, TightVNC, curl, Vim) after initial access — including through supply chain compromise of the DAEMON Tools installer.
incidents.impact: Long-term persistent access established in targeted networks across telecommunications organizations, universities, medical nonprofits, government contractors, and intergovernmental organizations globally since at least October 2025; malware designed for sustained intelligence collection with modular extensibility.

incidents.vector: FSB-linked operators deployed fully automated AI-driven workflows to orchestrate an end-to-end cyber espionage campaign against Ukrainian targets with minimal human operator involvement.
incidents.impact: Significantly expanded intelligence collection volume against Ukrainian targets; AI orchestration allowed the group to absorb higher operational security failures in exchange for dramatically increased intelligence throughput from compromised networks.

incidents.victim: Millions of Chrome users (Poper Blocker / Big Star Labs)
incidents.vector: Poper Blocker, a spyware-laced Chrome extension carrying a Google-verified 'Featured' badge, deploys an obfuscated C2 downloader that activates after 24 hours and silently exfiltrates browsing data, screenshots, and AI chatbot conversation histories.
incidents.impact: Over 2 million active users' full browsing histories, AI chat sessions (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini), screenshots, and location data sold to third parties; related Big Star Labs extensions add ~2 million more affected users. Google has not removed the app despite researcher notification since May 2026.

incidents.vector: A suspected autonomous AI agent breached the internal systems of the Dutch non-profit that coordinates responsible vulnerability disclosure on behalf of security researchers.
incidents.impact: Internal systems compromised; scope under investigation. The breach highlights AI-driven attacks targeting security organizations — DIVD plans to publish technical findings publicly.

incidents.vector: A departing Federal Reserve Board employee allegedly removed confidential Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) information from the institution upon their departure.
incidents.impact: Sensitive monetary policy deliberations potentially exfiltrated; the Fed's Inspector General issued an alert and is actively investigating. The nature and volume of the removed data have not been publicly disclosed.

incidents.vector: Russian military drone strikes directly targeted Kyivstar's headquarters and data center facilities in Kyiv, Ukraine.
incidents.impact: Headquarters building and data centers of Ukraine's largest mobile telecommunications provider severely damaged; telecoms services disrupted across Ukraine. Physical attack on digital infrastructure in the context of ongoing hybrid warfare.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters re-exploited CVE-2026-35273 in Oracle PeopleSoft, adapting to bypass published WAF workarounds issued by Mandiant, and deployed web shells on dozens of systems across organizations that implemented workarounds but had not applied the full patch.
incidents.impact: Confirmed data theft across higher education, technology, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, and government sectors globally; dozens of organizations now face extortion threats and potential public exposure of HR, payroll, and student records databases.

incidents.vector: Two zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-88771: command injection; CVE-2026-88772: memory overflow) in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway allow unauthenticated remote code execution and have been actively exploited globally since at least September 24 with a proof-of-concept now publicly available.
incidents.impact: Over 50,000 publicly exposed instances identified as potentially vulnerable; multiple organizations worldwide confirmed compromised before patches released September 27. CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and mandated federal agency patching within 72 hours. Citrix's delayed 36-hour public communication while exploitation was active drew sharp industry criticism.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited CVE-2026-35273 in Oracle PeopleSoft to access the FBI's job application portal, defaced the site with an ASCII art message, and exfiltrated agent employment records.
incidents.impact: Personal data, psychiatric and medical records, duty assignments, and family information for more than 5,000 FBI officials stolen and sampled to media. Experts warn the dataset provides a roadmap for state actors and criminal organizations to physically target individual agents. The FBI acknowledges it is 'operating under the premise' that data on all FBI employees was exfiltrated. The FBI jobs site remains offline.

incidents.vector: Iranian state operators use WhatsApp and Telegram to build rapport before delivering CHOSEN BRICK Windows spyware disguised as legitimate applications (Pictory, Norton Antivirus, Telegram, fake MRI scan results) via social engineering.
incidents.impact: CHOSEN BRICK collects contacts, emails, social media messages, screen captures, and microphone audio; victim personal details have appeared on pro-Iranian leak sites, creating physical safety risks. Targets confirmed in the UK, US, and Netherlands. Joint advisory by NCSC, FBI, and Dutch AIVD.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an SQL injection vulnerability in the Medyc electronic health records platform interface in late August 2026 and exfiltrated an encrypted archive of patient databases.
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 5 million patients stolen, including names, national IDs, addresses, and likely medical records from addiction and psychiatric treatment centers; the same actor linked to the larger MyDr breach. Polish data protection authority has ordered an audit of Qbusoft.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an unspecified vulnerability in MyDr, which connects Polish healthcare providers to the nation's centralized electronic health system for prescriptions, referrals, and patient records.
incidents.impact: Approximately 19 million patient records from 12,000 healthcare organizations potentially compromised — one of the largest healthcare breaches in European history. Likely carried out by the same actor responsible for the subsequent Medyc breach.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense (Defense Manpower Data Center)
incidents.vector: A misconfigured file-sharing system at the Defense Manpower Data Center exposed military personnel records online without access controls for approximately nine months (October 2025 to July 2026).
incidents.impact: Names, military information, and Social Security numbers of DMDC members confirmed accessed by unauthorized parties during the exposure window. Pentagon has begun notifying affected individuals.

incidents.vector: JadePuffer (China-suspected, tracked as Storm-3168) compromised two Azure service principals whose credentials had been inadvertently exposed in a public GitHub issue edit history, then orchestrated an AI-automated reconnaissance and destruction campaign.
incidents.impact: Over 100 Azure storage accounts deleted, plus Key Vault, Function Apps, and App Service plans wiped in a rapid destructive campaign consistent with ransomware extortion — though no ransom note was confirmed. Microsoft identified the group has been probing multiple Azure App services across other customers since January 2026.

incidents.vector: Fraudsters used AI voice cloning to impersonate the Intesa Sanpaolo CEO and a lawyer in communications with the Fideuram chairman, directing wire transfers to Chinese and Hong Kong bank accounts.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108M) transferred fraudulently; Intesa Sanpaolo recovered the majority but €36 million remains missing. One of the largest AI-enabled financial fraud cases on record.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters social-engineered an Odido employee via phone into logging into a spoofed authentication portal, capturing valid credentials to access internal systems and customer databases.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 6.2 million Dutch people stolen from the Netherlands' largest mobile telecom provider. A Dutch suspect linked to the operation was arrested in September 2026; ShinyHunters threatened further large-scale attacks against Dutch organizations in response.
